claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a solid solution.
A mild oxidation pretreatment will form a controlled submonolayer oxide on the catalyst surface.
The submonolayer surface oxide modifies the local electronic structure of active sites.
The submonolayer surface oxide modifies the geometric configurations of active sites.
The submonolayer oxide alters the binding energies of ethanol and its oxidation intermediates.
The oxide-modified interface lowers barriers along the pathway to the desired oxidation product.
The oxide-modified interface suppresses competing side reactions.
Favoring preferred intermediate evolution over competing pathways increases product selectivity.
Under identical ethanol-oxidation conditions, the oxidation-pretreated catalyst will show greater selectivity toward a desired product such as acetic acid than the untreated catalyst.

The proposed effect is expected within typical ethanol-oxidation potential, temperature, and electrolyte ranges, provided bulk oxidation, severe restructuring, and stability-limit exceedance are avoided.
